caption: The phase-3 Ashen Knight after turning on the spot to face the gate lens: facing confirmed by bone check, but at noon from the gate it is backlit and reads as a dark silhouette (GL frame).

Hero from behind at rest: the furled glider is now a compact roll inside the hips instead of a bar jutting out at the elbows; the hero still stands in the cottage's shade and this is a GL frame, not Forward+.
End of the stepped standing turn, face to the lens, arms relaxed and staff slung; flat GL lighting in shade, so it does not yet hold up as a Wukong frame.
Mid stepped turn from above: the inside foot stays planted while the outside foot steps round and the body swings over it; GL frame in tree shade, so the light is flat.
End of the pivot turn, square to the lens with the feet still staggered before the idle settles; flat GL shade lighting, not a Forward+ frame.
The Ashen Knight (phase-1 size) mid-turn on the spot, stepping round on a planted foot; GL frame, backlit at 15:00 so the knight is a silhouette and the plant can't be judged closely.

The hero standing across a 23 deg hillside with the new foot IK: hips settled, both boots meet the turf at their own height; GL frame from the front along the contour, so the difference is subtle and the lighting is not Forward+.
The same spot without foot IK for comparison: the clip stands as on flat ground and the far boot hangs over the downhill side; GL frame.
The Ashen Knight still on its knee as the surge bursts, glaive heaved skyward inside the ring of fire; backlit from the gate so the flung-back head is only a silhouette, GL frame.
The knight risen at its phase-2 size, glaive levelled back into guard with the fire still burning; the fallen stone in front reads blocky and the figure is backlit, GL frame.

Toe IK test: a boot stands on top of a 16 cm masonry block with nothing sunk into it; the lens is not side-on so the ball-on-edge read is unverified, and the GL quick-look lighting and test block are not shipping quality.

The hero stepping off a 0.3 m masonry course: one boot still on the tread, the other set down on the turf with no fall; the lens sits behind instead of side-on and the hero is in tree shade, GL frame.

0.05 s into a stagger from the Hollow soldier's thrust: the hero's chest caves round the blow and the head drops while the hips give back; the cloak hides most of the body line and this is a GL quick-look, not Forward+.
0.2 s into the stagger: the hero has stepped back about a metre on real backward steps (no skating) and is rebounding upright; the reaction is readable but modest at this distance.

A Hollow soldier 0.07 s after a blow from ahead: the chest caves round it, the head is thrown forward and the spear knocked up, reacting at the joints instead of tipping as one rigid piece; GL quick-look in cottage shade, no Forward+ frame yet.
The same stagger at 0.15 s: the shove walked off in a real backward step into a wide stance while the spear comes back to guard; flat GL light, and the cloak hides the hip throw.

GL quick-look: a Hollow soldier shoved from its right swings its legs round into the stumble while the chest counter-twists to keep the spear on the hero; the boots are lost in the tall grass so the planted-foot pivot cannot be judged by eye, and this is GL compatibility, not Forward+.

GL quick-look: mid-unwind of the side stagger, the soldier squaring back up toward the hero; still wrong: the grass hides the feet, the fixed lens lets the soldier drift out of frame, and the conical hood reads blocky.
A Hollow soldier mid-stumble from a side blow (0.17 s in): the stance boot is now pinned by the contact lock while it backs off the shove; GL quick-look, still in the cottage's shade.
The same stumble at 0.25 s: legs stepped back under the body on bare turf, chest counter-twisted; needs a sunlit Forward+ frame and the soldier drifts to the frame edge.

A Hollow soldier 0.15 s into a side-blow reel: chest twisted off the blow, boots stepping back wide with the stance boot now also held sideways; GL quick-look, flat light and the cottage shade still darken it.
The same reel at 0.45 s: stepped 0.66 m off the line and turning back to the hero, spear dropping to guard, feet planted; still a GL frame, not a sunlit Forward+ one.

GL quick-look: the hero mid-run on open turf with the new sideways foot lock; the figure is small and backlit, its feet in its own shadow, so the planted boot cannot be judged by eye here, and this is GL compatibility, not Forward+.
GL quick look: the hero mid-sprint with the planted boot held (skeleton modifiers now run once per physics tick); still 3/4 from behind with the legs in the cottage shade, not a Forward+ frame.

GL quick look: the hero mid-sprint leaning into the stride with the staff slung (the sprint's landing boot now eases onto its strike point, worst slip 0.051 -> 0.039 m/tick); the lens sits behind the hero and the long grass hides the feet, not a Forward+ frame.
The boss reveal's dormant beat: slumped over its planted glaive, head bowed (GL frame; Forward+ not checked, the blade tip hovers just above the turf).
The boss reveal's roar beat: glaive heaved up, chest and head thrown back (GL frame from its back flank; the face is hidden, needs a front-lit Forward+ frame).
The dormant boss leans on its glaive with the point now meeting the turf by its right boot (GL quick look, not Forward+); the bowed head does not read under the helm.
The roar beat from the knight front: the glaive is up but the head throw and chest-out barely read from straight on; needs a stronger back arch or a lower 3/4 lens.
The knight's roar from its sunlit flank: helm and shoulders arched back behind planted hips, glaive raised; GL fallback frame (no fog/GI), the glaive is still forward of vertical.
The dormant knight from the flank, hunched through the spine over its planted glaive; back-lit, the body reads as a dark silhouette.
The Ashen Knight's reveal roar with the deeper back arch: helm thrown back, glaive carried straight up in both hands; GL fallback frame (Vulkan OOM), no fog/GI, lens not truly on the flank.
The knight's gather before the roar: knees set, glaive drawn back low; GL fallback frame, flat lighting.

The Ashen Knight (first size) mid-turn on the spot, its trailing boot lifted in the new step arc instead of scraping; GL frame, the knight is backlit and its feet too small and dark to read the arc well.
The knight squaring up to the gate at the end of its turn with the glaive carried across; GL compatibility lighting, flat dark armour and a bare dirt floor, not Wukong quality yet.

The Ashen Knight turning on the spot, seen low from the gate: its trailing boot is lifted clear of the turf mid-step in one arc. Still wrong: GL lighting, the armour reads near-black in its own shade and the lens crops the body.
Four ticks later the boot comes round low and sets down flat, nothing sunk into the turf. Still wrong: GL frame, dark armour, no Forward+ light on the legs.
Knight at size 2.2 mid turn step from the gate, low: the trailing boot is up and swinging round; GL frame, armour near-black in its own shade, speckled ground is a GL artefact.
Same turn eight frames later: the boot is braking into the turf beside the planted one and sets down flat instead of tapping down; still GL lighting, lens crops above the belt.

Forward+ frame of the Ashen Knight (size 2.2) turning on the spot, boots planted mid-step; still wrong: the ring floor is a flat grey with cartoon black speckles and the low lens crops the knight at the shoulders.

The hero turning on the spot toward the lens, head leading, the stepping boot carried in one 4 cm arc (bot-measured); still wrong: GL lighting, the feet are hidden under the tabard in shade, so the arc is not visible from this high lens.
Same turn 0.6 s later, squared to the lens with the stepping boot easing down; still wrong: the end stance is left staggered with no settle step, dark GL turf and lens too high to read the soles.

The hero just after a turn on the spot, squared up with both feet stepped into the idle stance (GL frame); the boots are lost in shade under the tabard, the hands hang claw-like and the lighting is a flat GL fallback.
The knight (size 2.2) squared up after a turn on the spot, both boots settled under it in the idle stance (GL quick-look frame, not Forward+); the ring floor still reads as flat speckled dirt.

The hero's right hand at rest, before (left) and after (right): fingers drawn together and curled in a relaxed cascade instead of the clip's stiff splay (GL quick-look, not Forward+); the glove's knuckle plates still read a little blocky.
Staff drawn, before (left) and after (right): the lower hand now closes into a fist round the shaft instead of splaying open over it (GL quick-look, low resolution).

Hollow soldier's hands on the spear, before (left: clip fingers splayed open over the shaft, a claw on the lower hand) and after (right: both hands closed into fists round the haft); GL quick-look, the lens is too close and the gauntlets still read blocky.

A Hollow soldier's right fist now closed round the spear haft (the wrist moved off the shaft so it runs through the fingers); GL quick-look, the hand sits in shadow and the lens still does not centre on it.

GL quick-look of the Ashen Knight's left fist on the glaive through the new own-lens close-up: the framing now holds, but the lens sits behind the knight and the fist is a dark shape in shadow at the right of the frame.

GL frame of light-string blow 2 frozen mid-swing (the swing shot spot works again): the staff sweeps level at shoulder height, but the fixed lens loses the hero's hands as the body spins away and GL lighting is flat
GL frame of blow 2's wind-up, staff carried back over the right shoulder; the hands are too small and dark to judge the grip: needs a close lens that follows the spin and a Forward+ render

The phase-2 knight holding its stomp's knee-up, hips now shifted over the standing boot (GL quick-look); still wrong: the front lens is backlit at 15:00 and the tall grass hides both boots, so the weight shift cannot be judged in this frame.

The Ashen Knight buckled in the crown reel, glaive drooping into the turf, its boots now held where they stood (bot-proven); still backlit against the sun, so the legs read as a silhouette (GL frame).
The knight shaking off the crown reel and standing straight again after its settle steps; backlit silhouette, the ground under it is flat dark dirt (GL frame).
The knight down on its right knee in the growth surge, left boot now held where it stood (bot-proven); backlit silhouette, and the falling grit draws as big black lens blobs (GL frame).

The Ashen Knight's growth surge with its ring of fire: the soot off the flame columns is now lit grey smoke, no longer big black blots across the sky (GL frame); still wrong: the columns read as thin pale orange streaks with no hot core, and the shot is backlit.
The knight's growth-surge ring of fire 0.25 s after the burst: each column now has a white-hot core with orange licks instead of pale streaks (GL frame; Forward+ ran out of memory this session).
0.6 s after the burst the columns lick down and charcoal smoke finally shows above them; one centre puff is still a round soft blob.
The knight at size 3 in its second growth surge, seen from a lens now kept on the ring's open floor; the ring of fire reads well, but the smoke plume is too faint and the lens shows its back.
Growth surge 0.9 s after the burst: the smoke over the columns no longer balls into one blob, but now only a few thin wisps show against the sky.

The Ashen Knight's growth surge now seen from its front (cracked glowing helm, red tabard, the village behind) with the ring of fire round it; the nearest flame columns blur across the lens and the smoke plume is still thin.
Ashen Knight growth surge 2 s after the ring of fire: the column smoke now drifts as translucent grey plumes instead of black blots; still a little flat and brownish, and the lighting is dim.
The ring of fire bursting round the kneeling Ashen Knight, HUD hidden and the lens clear of the columns; fire reads well, the helm's glowing cracks look like cartoon eyes.

Close on the Ashen Knight's helm and pauldrons mid-surge: the ember glow now runs in sparse, tapering, irregular seams instead of two eye-like blobs; frame is from behind (the lens front score is inverted) and fire reflections smear orange over the helm.

The grown knight in the stone ring at the end of a surge: cracked plate glows faintly at the helm and pauldrons, smoke drifts over the ring; still seen from its back and GL-only, not a Forward+ frame.

The Ashen Knight's reveal at the gather beat (GL): it now coils the glaive low on its right side, knees set, before the heave, instead of lifting it into a raised crouch; the knight stands in shadow and it is not a Forward+ frame.
The reveal's follow-through (GL): the glaive comes down beside the helm so the visor and its ember seams stay visible; the turf around the ring still reads flat and speckled.

The Ashen Knight's reveal heave, front lens (GL): the glaive now swings out and up round its right side from the coil instead of through its chest; the knight still stands in the stones' shadow and the frame is GL, not Forward+.
A beat later the shaft rises diagonally to its right shoulder on the way to the skyward roar; the body still reads stiff at the hips and the lighting is flat GL.

The Ashen Knight's reveal coil (GL frame, it=2.95): chest twisted to its right, a fist low at the right hip and the glaive trailing low behind, so the heave is an upward sweep; still a GL frame, and the head turns away with the chest instead of staying on the hero.
The heave out of the new coil (GL, it=3.1): the glaive rises diagonally round the knight's right side; lighting is still the flat GL path, not Forward+.
The Ashen Knight's reveal coil (GL frame): chest twisted round to its right, glaive trailing low, helm held on the hero; still lit flat in the stones' shadow and only a GL frame.
The coil in profile (the kside lens now works): crouched, glaive low behind the right hip; backlit to a silhouette, GL not Forward+.

The reveal lens at the roar: the glaive now stands upright beside the helm, blade to the sky, no fist across the visor; the fists are hidden behind the thrown-back helm from this lens, GL not Forward+.
The roar in profile: arm raised above the helm, glaive vertical on its right instead of both hands hugging the visor; backlit to a silhouette in the stones' shadow, GL only.

Reveal heave mid-rise (GL): the glaive now sweeps up beside the knight's right shoulder instead of across its chest; the knight still stands in the stones' shadow and the GL frame lacks Forward+ fog/GI.
Reveal heave at it=3.13 (GL): the glaive now stands upright on the knight's right side instead of crossing its body with the butt at the left hip; the knight is still backlit in the stones' shadow.
Reveal heave at it=3.20 (GL): the glaive rises beside the helm with both fists climbing the haft; the knight still reads as a dark silhouette against the sun.

Boss reveal coil, front-lit at 08:30 (GL frame): glaive drawn low at the right hip, helm on the hero; the giant reads well-lit for the first time, but the frame is GL (Forward+ OOM-killed) and the knight is small in the lens.
Boss reveal heave, front-lit (GL): the glaive stands upright on its right, but the shaft still crosses the right edge of the helm in this lens.
Boss reveal roar in profile, lit (GL): fist raised and glaive skyward, but the flung-back head is hidden behind the raised arm and the hood, so it reads as a hunch, not a roar.

Boss reveal roar (GL, hour 8.5): the left hand now lets go of the haft and is thrown up in a fist while the glaive stands skyward in the right; the flung-back helm still reads as a dark dome, the face never shows.
Close front lens on the roar: raised fist and glaive frame the knight's shoulders; the fingers look half open rather than clenched and the frame is GL, not Forward+.

The Ashen Knight's raised roar hand, close (GL): before, a hooked half-open claw with a hole through it; now the fingers fold tight into the palm. Still wrong: the thumb points up along the index instead of wrapping across the fingers.
The knight's left fist thrown up against the sky at the top of the reveal roar (GL, hour 8.5); reads as a fist at this distance, thumb still upright, armour hand texture plain.
Close-up of the knight's raised roar fist: the fingers fold tight, but the thumb still stands upright beside the index (5 aim-based fixes tried this session, none looked better).
BEFORE (env CLIMB_NOSQUARE): climbing the keep with the staff guard's 44 deg pelvis turn still on, the back and robe panel angled off the stones; the wall's shadow hides most of the figure.

AFTER: hips and chest square to the stones, left hand reaching for the next hold, knee up, the back panel hanging straight down the wall; still dim in the wall's shadow, the climb moves at an even speed with no push/pull surge.

The hero mid-climb on the keep's outer face (GL, 15:30): arms reaching hand over hand, head tipped up the face; the body now surges between reaches, but the whole face still sits in the wall's own shadow so the figure reads as a dark silhouette.
The hero climbing the keep seen from behind, hips swung out over the standing foot; GL frame, the figure is still small and the wall face is flatly lit.
Same climb frame before (left, hips centred) and after (right, belt tipped, hips and robe out over the standing foot, shoulders level); weight shift reads but is subtle.

Hero on the keep's stones from behind with the right foot stepping up: the belt and robe tip up on the stepping hip while the chest stays level; GL frame, the figure is small and in the face's shadow, no Forward+.
Before (level pelvis, left) and after (stepping hip hiked, right) close crop: belt tilt is visible but subtle; the hands, glide and deep-hold lean-in are still rough.

Hero climbing the keep from behind mid-step with the new frog step: the stepping knee swings out past the robe panel; GL frame, the figure is small and in the face's shadow and the panel hides the thighs.
Before (knee in line, left) and after (frog step, right) close crop: the right knee sits a few cm further out; subtle from this lens, needs a lit three-quarter view.

Knock-down get-up 1.25 s in: the hero now rolls onto the near hip propped on a hand planted in the turf, knees drawn up, instead of a symmetric sit-up with hands floating; GL frame, lens high and grass hides the hand.
Knock-down get-up 1.42 s in: the hand lets go as the hero comes over the feet into the squat; the rise is still one symmetric squat with no knee-down step.

Knock-down get-up: the hero now kneels on the left knee with the right foot planted ahead before rising, instead of a two-footed squat; the legs are still half hidden in the tall grass and the free right arm just hangs.
Mid-rise from the kneel: the front leg drives the body up and the back knee leaves the turf; the reaching left arm and hanging right arm still need weight-bearing poses.

Knock-down rise, grass hidden: before (1.62, hand hanging by the shin) / after (1.62, right palm braced on the front knee) / after (1.74, pushing off the thigh); the left hand still claws out in front of the chest.
The kneeling rise in the meadow at 15:30: tall grass hides the braced hand and knees; the figure reads as kneeling but the frame is cluttered by foreground blades.

Knock-down rise, grass hidden, 1.62/1.70/1.76: before (top) the free left hand claws out in front of the chest; after (bottom) it hangs by the hip as a counterweight. The hang still splays a little to the side.
Kneeling up at 1.70 in the GL fallback: right palm on the front knee, left arm hanging by the thigh; the GL frame lacks fog and GI so it is not a Wukong-grade image.
Standing up after a knock-down: the free left hand now hangs as a loose half-curl instead of a splayed claw; GL fallback lighting is flat and the arm still swings up to the guard quickly.
Kneel in the knock-down rise: right palm on the front knee, left hand loose by the hip; GL compatibility render, no fog or GI, so not yet a Wukong frame.
Knock-down sit-up BEFORE (down_t 1.40, front lens): the knees are drawn up to the chest and both boots hang 0.3-0.4 m in the air by the seat.
Knock-down sit-up AFTER: the soles stay planted on the turf with the shins down to them; still a front lens that foreshortens the legs, and the flung staff floats in the air at the left.

Knock-down rise (down_t 1.70): the hero keeps the staff in the right fist, its butt planted on the turf by the front knee, pushing up on it instead of the staff hanging in mid-air; GL frame, the lens still foreshortens the legs.
Just after the get-up (1.95): the staff comes back up from the right fist to the guard beside the body; the left hand has not caught it yet in this mid-regrip frame (rough).

End of the knock-down rise (down_t 1.84): the free left hand has left the hip and closed on the staff's grip before the draw back to guard, instead of swinging in open from 0.25 m away; GL frame from behind, the guard line still reads low.
Close crop of the same frame: the left fist closed round the wrapped grip; the hand is clean but the body is still the rough get-up pose.

Rising from a knock-down at 1.74 s: the left hand is already closed on the staff's wrapped grip as the shaft is held upright beside the body; the staff top still runs close to the hat brim and the lens sees mostly the back.
Side-on at 1.33 s into a knock-down: the held staff now angles up in front of the face instead of swinging its top through the hat and head; the low backlit lens still leaves the body dark.
Side-on at 1.72 s: the staff stands on its butt beside the rising hero, clear of the hat brim; the get-up pose is still rough and backlit.

Side-on at 1.27 s into a knock-down, sun-lit: sitting up, the hero keeps the staff's far end trailing on the grass instead of holding it up across the face; the grip's short butt still pokes up beside the chest and the get-up pose is still rough.
1.00 s: the staff lies on the grass out to the hero's back-right, still in the right fist; GL frame, flat ground texture, no Forward+ lighting.

Knock-down get-up (GL): the staff now starts swinging up from the grass on the hero's right as they sit up, spread over 0.4 s instead of a two-tick whip; the body pose and the lit grass are still rough.
Knock-down get-up (GL): the staff stands planted by the knee clear of the hat; the hero's crouch still reads stiff and the GL frame has no fog or GI.
Knock-down get-up at 1.73 s: the held staff now waits at the hat's brim and comes round it instead of jerking out past it; seen from behind, grass off, body pose still rough.
Knock-down get-up at 1.90 s: the staff mid-way through the new eased half-second draw back to the guard, upright beside the body; lens behind the hero, grass off, ground texture still flat.

Knock-down get-up at 1.73 s: the held staff now steps round the hat brim and lies diagonally behind the left shoulder, well clear of the hat (it used to wait at the brim and then sweep through it in the draw); body pose still rough, flat ground texture.

Knock-down get-up at 1.80 s: the left fist is closed on the shaft by the hip and the staff runs low toward the guard instead of standing up through the hat; lens from behind, so the guard line is foreshortened.

Jump attack 0.16 s into the swing: the shins swing up behind and the legs trail as the staff climbs overhead; the clear+close jump lens sees the hero from behind with the head cropped, so the back arch cannot be judged here.

Jump attack at the arch peak, first front 3/4 frame: the trunk tips back and a shin trails, but the staff stands upright beside the hat instead of cocked behind the head, and the figure is dark against the grass.
Jump attack on the blow: face and hat read under the new air lens, staff struck down-forward, knees up; the fold is mild with the head still upright.
Jump attack at the arch's peak with the staff now cocked 26 deg behind the head, clear of the hat; from this rear-left lens it still reads near-upright, not a drawn bow.
Jump attack fold: head bowed under the hat over the down-swinging staff; the fold is still mild and the dark trousers merge with the grass.

Jump attack at the arch's peak, side lens: the head now tips over and the staff is drawn back ~40 deg past vertical behind the hat (was 26); still wrong: the left hand reads open beside the brim and the figure is backlit and dark.
Same instant from the rear 3/4 lens: the tilted hat shows, but from behind the deeper draw still reads as an upright staff; the move needs a side-on gameplay camera to sell the bow.

Jump attack at the arch's peak, staff snatched off the back: both fists now closed on the shaft over the hat; still seen from behind, so the drawn-back cock reads as a staff held across rather than a loaded bow.
Same moment before the fix: both open hands reach up beside the hat while the staff still lags across the back (slow 0.22 s air snatch plus trunk bends carrying the arms off).

Jump attack mid-snatch, side-on: the staff swings off the back across the shoulders with the right fist already on it; backlit, the figure reads as a silhouette and the left hand is still rising from the hip.

Jump attack at the top of the arch from a slung start: the staff is drawn ~39 deg back behind the hat with the right fist on the shaft; still backlit to a silhouette, and the cottage behind reads plain.

Hero halting from a run with the staff drawn at guard: both fists stay on the shaft through the stop's hip and back bend (they used to ride 20 cm off); backlit, the figure is a silhouette and the foreground is black.

Mid-run at guard: the staff held low and diagonal in both fists with the chest now square to it (the right fist no longer slides off); seen from behind, the dog overlaps the legs and the lens doesn't show the face.
Guard run with the staff drawn, square side-on (new sidelens, dog hidden): forward lean, back knee high, staff carried low and forward in both fists; still a backlit silhouette in GL, no Forward+.
Same stride from the sun side: the capelet and hood hide the chest and face, so the squared chest reads as a back view; legs and staff read, the dog crowds the legs.

Guard run with the staff drawn, seen from ahead (new frontlens, dog hidden): chest square, staff carried diagonally across the body with both fists together on its upper third, hat and masked face toward the camera; backlit at 10:00 so the front is in shade, GL renderer.
Same run at 16:30 from ahead: the face under the hat now reads, but the hero runs in the cottage's shadow and the lit meadow is behind; the pose holds up, the light does not.

Jump attack at jt 0.38 (front 3/4 from the shadow side): staff swinging over and forward in both fists, hat and capelet read; the robe's straight red panels hide the tucked legs so the airborne body reads stiff, and the GL backlight leaves the hero a silhouette.

Jump attack fold at jt 0.48: body jackknifed over the blow, the staff driven down to the grass ahead, face under the hat reads; one robe panel sticks out as a flat, stiff red blade instead of trailing like cloth.
Jump attack at jt 0.38 BEFORE: the staff has already swung past vertical in front while the chest still leans 14 deg back and the face looks at the sky, so the body trails the blow.
Same frame AFTER the body leads the staff: head and hat over the fists, face down on the target, chest coming forward; still GL-only and backlit at 11:00, legs hang under the hips at this tick.

Jump attack fold, before (left) and after (right): the robe's front panel used to hang as a flat red board hiding the tucked legs; it now lies along the thigh and folds down at the knee so the tucked boot shows. Still GL-only, rear 3/4, crease at the knee reads a little sharp.
Jump attack at jt 0.48 with the knee fold: panel over the thigh, hem hanging plumb from the knee, legs read as tucked; figure small and backlit in GL.
Jump attack fold, hard crease (left) vs the new rolled knee fold (right): the robe panel now curves over the knee instead of turning a square corner. Still GL-only, rear 3/4 and backlit.
Jump attack fold at jt 0.52 with the rolled knee fold; the figure is small and in shadow and the red panel still reads too saturated.

0.74 s after the jump-attack press the hero is already back upright with the staff on the shoulder and the robe hanging; this frame missed the new falling-robe landing, which is bot-checked only so far (GL render, backlit, figure small).

The jump attack 0.10 s before touch-down: legs tucked, staff driven down; from this rear-3/4 lens only the back robe panel shows, so the new falling front panel still is not seen (GL render, backlit, red too flat).
